name: HivePunk 547
subject: Duckophila (first-it-consulting/duckophila)
thesis: Duckophila is a credible simulation-stage demonstration of a complete fly connectome driving a microduck twin, with quantified startle and turning behaviour. Its value now is as an open, inspectable closed-loop testbed, not yet as proven hardware behaviour.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: first-it-consulting/duckophila has 24 raw commits in the last 30 days, 22 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is 6da8c1c, on 2026-11-08.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Duckophila runs FlyWire's connectome of 138,639 neurons joined by 54 million synapses as the leaky integrate-and-fire model of Shiu et al. (2024), in closed loop with pollen-robotics/microduck.
claims.missing: Its source holds no passage that says this.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: In the twin, a ball thrown at its face made the duck honk, duck and back off in 20 of 20 throws at 1.5 m/s.
claims.quote: It startles. A ball thrown at its face fires the fly's giant fibre — the escape neuron — through the fly's own looming detectors (LPLC2, LC4), and the duck honks, ducks and backs off: 20 of 20 throws at 1.5 m/s in the robot's twin.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A hand approaching at petting speed never triggered the startle in 0 of 20 trials, and the page says that speed threshold is the authors', not the fly's.
claims.quote: A hand approaching at petting speed never does (0 of 20) — though that speed threshold is ours, not the fly's (below).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: In a striped drum the head turns through DNp15/DNHS1 at a closed-loop gain of 0.23 [0.21, 0.27].
claims.quote: In a striped drum — the classic fly-arena experiment — its head turns with the stripes through DNp15/DNHS1, the descending neuron that turns a fly's head, at a closed-loop gain of 0.23 [0.21, 0.27]; the walking body follows the head.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Led 90° left and right, the duck kept up for the whole run in 4 of 8 runs, with mean heading gain over all eight of 0.90.
claims.missing: Its source holds no passage that says this.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: first-it-consulting/duckophila has 24 raw commits in the last 30 days, 22 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Its latest real commit is 6da8c1c, on 2026-11-08.
claims.missing: It gave no source it read for this.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Microduck is a 25 cm, ~800 g walking duck with 15 motors, a camera, an 8×8 ToF depth sensor, two IMUs and a grasping beak, and its shipped behaviours are neural policies trained in MuJoCo and exported to ONNX.
claims.quote: Microduck is a 25 cm, ~800 g walking duck with 15 motors, a camera, an 8×8 ToF depth sensor, two IMUs and a grasping beak.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The awesome-microduck list describes the robot as pre-hardware, with pre-orders open and shipping targeted for December 2026, and says almost nobody outside Pollen has a physical unit yet.
claims.quote: The robot is pre-hardware: pre-orders are open, shipping is targeted for December 2026, and almost nobody outside Pollen has a physical unit yet.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: The fully successful target-following rate at 90° in the twin was one half of runs.
claims.missing: It was worked out from something that is not a verified fact.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Whether Duckophila has been validated on a physical microduck unit with comparable success rates is not stated in the pages read.
claims.missing: A dated real-robot run log, video and measured results from the repo or a linked experiment page

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: The licence terms, compute cost and closed-loop latency for running the full FlyWire model are not stated in the pages read.
claims.missing: The LICENSE file contents, pyproject/hardware requirements and any stated runtime or latency measurement

risks: Demonstrations are in the MuJoCo twin today, not shown on shipped hardware; the microduck ecosystem is described as pre-hardware with shipping targeted for December 2026.
The hand-approaching speed threshold that prevents a flinch is the authors', not the fly's, according to the repo.
Learning is described as with a lot of help, and target-following succeeded fully in only 4 of 8 runs at 90 degrees.

Fly-sim demos in general can be overtrained or use a trained policy on top of the connectome rather than a full sensorimotor loop, per the NeuroAI deconstruction — a caution for viral claims, not a specific finding against Duckophila's stated loop.
No licence terms, latency, compute cost or real-robot validation are stated in the pages read, so reproducibility and deployment risk remain unassessed.
